title: `st.iframe` hardcodes the frame title, so every embed on a page has the same accessible name
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary The `

comments.body:
**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16607)

This is a valid accessibility bug, not a duplicate. `st.iframe`, `st.components.v1.iframe`, and `st.components.v1.html` all render through the same frontend `IFrame` component, which hardcodes `title="st.iframe"`. An iframe’s accessible name comes from that attribute, so multiple embeds on one page are announced identically (WCAG 2.2 4.1.2). The IFrame protobuf currently only carries `src`/`srcdoc`, `scrolling`, and `tab_index` — there is no `title` field, and none of the three Python APIs accept one. `tabIndex` is already forwarded from proto to the element, so an optional `title` (defaulting to `"st.iframe"`) would follow the same pattern without changing existing apps. Custom components v1 already set `title={componentName}` on their iframes, so they are not affected in the same way.

### Related Issues

- [#16148](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16148) — Fullscreen toolbar buttons also use a hard-coded accessible name, so screen-reader users cannot tell which image or chart each control belongs to. Same class of duplicate-name a11y failure.
- [#8563](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8563) — Request for `alt_text` on images and charts so assistive tech can distinguish visual content. Parallel gap: embedded content has no author-supplied accessible name.
- [#8399](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8399) — Broader request for basic web accessibility (page language, named structure). This iframe-title gap is a concrete instance of that theme.

Related to: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8563 we should probably also provide an `alt` parameter for `st.iframe` that sets this attribute. st.components.v1.iframe and st.components.v1.html are both deprecated, so unlikely that we will apply changes to those commands.
